THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
ORDER Heard Sri Vitthal S.Teli, learned counsel for the petitioner, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1-State and Sri Sadanand M.K., learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the records on admission.

2. The present petition is filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. with the following prayer :-
"To quash proceedings in C.C.No.723/2021 as initiated and filed charge sheet by the Market Police, Belagavi under their P.S.Cr.No.347/2018, (P.C.No.270/2015) for the offences punishable u/sec. 465, 468, 471, 419, 420 r/w sec. 34 of IPC

initiated against the petitioner/accused no. 2 and the same is pending on the file of II J.M.F.C.
Belagavi."

3. The brief facts of the case are as under :-
2 n d respondent filed a private complaint on the file of II Addl.J.M.F.C., Belagavi against Sri Sanjay s/o Ramchandra Shivappanavar, Sri Ramchandra Vithappa Shivappanavar and Sri Prakash A.Koparde U/sec.200 Cr.P.C. alleging the commission of the offences punishable U/sec.177, 191, 192, 196, 198, 199, 200, 420,
463, 464, 468, 470 of IPC.

It is contended in the complaint that in the month of Shivaleela D/O Basavaraj Alias ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4777801/
2 September, 2015, daughter of the complainant was studying in M.Sc. at Rani Channamma University, Bhutramanahatti was found missing and a missing complaint was lodged with Kakati Police Station on 10.09.2015. Thereafter accused No.1 and complainant daughter appeared before the Kakati Police on 12.09.2015 and informed the investigation agency that daughter of the complainant Shivaleela married the 1 s t accused and their marriage was also registered on 16.05.2011.
4.

sentences.text:
On further enquiry, by the complainant with the Registrar of Marriages, Belagavi, he obtained certified copy of Form No.1 i.e. memorandum of marriage and certification registration of Hindu marriage and was supposed to note that his name has been appearing in Column No.6 wherein he has been shown as one of the witnesses to the marriage that took place on 06.05.2011 at 12.35 p.m.
at Veerabhadra Temple, Police Headquarters, Belagavi.
He was also shocked to note that his signature has been forged in the said column.
Complainant also contended that he was not a party to such a marriage and therefore sought for action against the all concerned.
Private complaint was referred to police by the jurisdictional Magistrate U/sec.156(3) of Cr.P.C. and thereafterwards the police enquired the matter in detail.
During the course of investigation, police have collected necessary information and also recorded the statement of 2 n d respondent.

Based on the material collected by the investigation agency, a charge sheet came to be filed by the police against Sri Sanjay Ramchandra Shivappanavar and the present petitioner who is the daughter of the complainant giving up Sri Ramchandra and Sri Prakash Koparde.
The learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offences alleged against the petitioner and Sri Sanjay.

5. Being aggrieved by the same, petitioner is before this Court with this petition seeking quashing of the order of taking cognizance and quashing of charge sheet which is now pending in C.C.No.723/2021.

6. Sri Vitthal S.Teli, learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently contended that the police instead of proceeding against Ramchandra and Prakash Koparde, filed charge sheet against the present petitioner and have come to the specific conclusion that it is the present petitioner who has forged the signature of her father in Column No.6 of Form No.1 and learned Magistrate took cognizance of the same without there being any proper material evidence on record especially in the absence of any statement made by the 2 n d respondent who is the complainant.

He also contended that the present petitioner had a love affair with the 1 s t accused and they have got married themselves before the Sub- Registrar and she is not aware who signed in Column No.6 as a witness to the registration of the marriage and sought for quashing of the charge sheet.

7. Per contra, learned HCGP while supporting the charge sheet contended that the police after thorough investigation based on the materials collected, came to the conclusion that the signature of the 2 n d respondent has been forged by the present petitioner in Form No.1 in Column No.6 and therefore, prima facie materials are available against the present petitioner to proceed against the present petitioner and Sanjay who is none other than the husband of the present petitioner.

8. She also contended that it is the 2nd petitioner who is the beneficiary of said forged signature and therefore, she has been rightly arraigned as an additional accused in the case and therefore sought Shivaleela D/O Basavaraj Alias ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4777801/
3 for rejection of the prayer of the petitioner.

sentences.text:
9. Learned counsel for defacto complainant however contended that after the marriage, there was a strained relationship between the present petitioner and the 1 s t accused Sanjay and it must be the Sanjay who has forged the signature of the 2 n d respondent and he has not stated before the police that it is his daughter who has forged the signature in Column No.6 of Form No.1 and therefore,
requested the court to pass appropriate order.

He also emphasized that having regard to the strained relationship, the present petitioner who is the daughter of the 2 n d respondent has left the company of the 1 s t accused and is now living with the 2 n d respondent and there are legal proceedings pending between the present petitioner and accused Sanjay before the Family Court as well as the before the criminal court for redressal of their respective grievances and therefore sought for passing of an appropriate order.
10.
In view of the rival contentions, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.
11. On such perusal of the material on record, it is seen that the complaint came to be filed by the 2 n d respondent as against Sanjay Ramchandra and Prakash Koparde.

However, the said private complaint was referred to the police for investigation and filing appropriate report by exercising power U/sec.156(3) of the Cr.P.C. by the learned jurisdictional Magistrate.

Police after receipt of such information, registered the case in Crime No.347/2018 on 30.12.2018 and investigated the matter thoroughly and filed the charge sheet against Sanjay and the present petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 465, 468, 471, 419, 420 read with 34 of IPC.
12.

While so filing the charge sheet, the second accused by name Ramchandra and third accused by name Prakash Koparde in private complaint have been dropped by the police, instead the present petitioner has been arraigned as accused No.2.
13.

Sri Vitthal S. Teli, learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently contended that the marriage of the present petitioner with first accused Sanjay was a love marriage and the same was also registered before the Sub-Registrar Office and she is not aware of the documents furnished to the Sub- Registrar Office and second respondent being shown as a witness and his signature being found in column No.6 of Form No.1 and therefore she is totally surprised by the action of the police.
. It is also argued that no report is available to form an opinion that it is the present petitioner who has forged the signature of second respondent.

15. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has also contended before the Court that he has not given any statement before the police stating that it is the present petitioner who has forged the signature of second respondent in column No.6 of Form No.1 which was produced before the Sub- Registrar Office.

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, in the absence of any independent material collected by the investigating agency, arraigning the present petitioner as the second accused and alleging that it is the present petitioner who has forged the signature of second respondent cannot be countenanced in law.

17. Learned High Court Government Pleader contended that the present petitioner is the - 11 - beneficiary of such forgery and therefore she has also been rightly arraigned as an accused by the investigating agency.
18. Assuming that the present petitioner is a beneficiary of the document that has been forged, only on that ground the present petitioner cannot be ordered to be proceeded with the criminal action.

More so when the second respondent himself has not stated that it is the present petitioner who has forged his signature in column No.6 of Form No.1.
19.
Under such circumstances, the proceeding against the present petitioner in C.C.No.723/2021 for the aforesaid offences would result in abuse of process of law.
Consequently, a case is made out for interference of this Court in taking cognizance and proceeding criminally against the present petitioner.

20. Accordingly, the following order is passed:
ORDER
Criminal petition is allowed.
- 12 - Pending proceedings as against the petitioner in C.C.No.723/2021 on the file of JMFC-II, Belagavi is hereby quashed.
This order shall not affect the rights of prosecution in proceeding against accused no.1 Sanjay.
